players.product: behind-the-meter natural-gas turbine power generation with balance of plant, batteries and O&M for data centers (Power Solutions)

quarterly_data.signal: Solaris's notes-offering memorandum (8-K): firm equipment orders with original equipment manufacturers put its power generation capacity on schedule to reach more than 3,300 MW by the end of 2029, from approximately 950 MW operated on average in Q2 2026; approximately 900 to 1,000 MW is currently not subject to long-term contracts. It expects consolidated capital expenditures of approximately $1,955 million for 2026 and estimates current and planned power generation investments at approximately $5 billion of aggregate capital. Power Solutions generated approximately 80% of Q2 2026 segment Adjusted EBITDA and is expected to exceed 90% upon full fleet deployment by the end of 2029.
quarterly_data.figure: >3,300 MW by end of 2029 (from ~950 MW); 2026 capex ~$1,955 million

quarterly_data.signal: Solaris's offering memorandum (8-K) contract summary, all predominantly fixed-fee for AI data center customers: Stateline (Solaris 50.1% equity) ~900 MW of off-grid power to a data center customer, executed Apr-2025, 7-year tenor, deliveries through Q1 2027; Hatchbo, LLC (affiliate of an investment-grade global technology company) executed Feb-2026 at approximately 530 MW, amended May-2026 and Jul-2026 into a turnkey ~660 MW plant, 10-year base plus 8-year option; Customer C (affiliate of an investment-grade technology company) executed April 24, 2026, ~640 MW including transformers, batteries and switchgear across multiple U.S. sites from the second half of 2026, 10 + 5-year option. Cancellation terms: Stateline 100% (Years 1-3) / 50% (Year 4+) of the remaining undiscounted revenue obligation; Hatchbo 50% plus 100% of remaining services payments (discounted); Customer C 50%. The three contracts provide approximately 2,200 MW; including energy and industrial users, more than 2,300 MW is under long-term contract.
quarterly_data.figure: ~900 MW + ~660 MW + ~640 MW (approximately 2,200 MW); >2,300 MW long-term contracted

quarterly_data.signal: Solaris's offering memorandum (8-K) on capacity sourcing: the Genco Acquisition (March 2026) adds approximately 400 MW of natural gas-fueled generation between 2026 and 2028, including approximately 100 MW operated and contracted; 30 turbine delivery slots secured in March 2026 from a private party add over 500 MW between early 2027 and 2029; two turbines secured in September 2026 from a private party for approximately $114.0 million add over 66 MW from Q1 2027; five turbines in Q2 2026 and one in Q3 2026 from a supplier add approximately 100 MW, subject to milestone payments. GESA added more than 1 GW of installed generation under O&M arrangements, and with GESA and Omega headcount rose from 468 employees at December 31, 2025 to more than 2,100; Omega makes Solaris less reliant on third-party EPC contractors for site preparation, heavy civil construction and substation development, a potential industry bottleneck.
quarterly_data.figure: Genco ~400 MW; 30 turbine slots >500 MW; 2 turbines >66 MW; 6 turbines ~100 MW
